title: Generative Model Based Standard Cell Timing Library Characterization
problem: Accurate cell timing characterization across PVT corners is essential for timing verification, but conventional SPICE simulation becomes prohibitively expensive as corner count explodes in modern designs, limiting scalability.
motivation: Post-Moore design complexity and corner explosion make traditional SPICE-based characterization inefficient; faster, scalable characterization methods are needed.
method: Uses a hybrid generative adversarial network (GAN) and autoencoder to learn and generalize timing arcs and corners, treating characterization as a generative modeling problem; the model learns distributions across timing arcs enabling efficient generation of corner timing data without expensive SPICE simulations.
key_novelty: Generative model approach (GAN + autoencoder hybrid) to standard cell timing library characterization, enabling high-accuracy, scalable prediction across corners.
contributions: Generative modeling perspective on timing library characterization
Hybrid GAN and autoencoder architecture for corner generalization
High accuracy timing prediction across PVT corners
Significant runtime reduction vs conventional SPICE-based approach
limitations: Not discussed; generative approach specifics not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: Generative model-based standard cell timing library characterization
